newsitem.title: USA: Bradley County, Tenn., public hospital sued.
newsitem.headline: Bradley County, Tenn., public hospital sued.

text.p: Two private medical groups have sued a hospital owned by Tennessee's Bradley County, claiming they face unfair competition as a result of partnerships the hospital entered into.

Cleveland Surgery Center LP and Ocoee Physical Therapy Inc said in the lawsuit that Bradley Memorial Hospital used joint ownership of various entities to "compete unfairly and unconstitutionally with the plaintiffs for the provision of health services."
A Bradley Memorial spokeswoman said Thursday that hospital officials could not comment on matters that are in litigation.
In addition to Bradley Memorial, the suit names a defendants Ocoee Health Alliance, Bradley Building LLC and the Bradley Healthcare Foundation.
The hospital created Bradley Building LLC to borrow $8.5 million to build the Bradley Medical Building, which is under construction on land adjacent to the hospital.
In creating Bradley Building LLC, admnistrators struck a deal that grants developers 25 percent ownership in the building and gives the hospital 75 percent, Presley said.
The hospital also owns 51 percent of Ocoee Health Alliance, with participating doctors owning the rest.
According to the lawsuit, the hospital has agreed to transfer a portion of the building ownership to doctors who lease and occupy space in it.

The act that created the hospital in 1947 prohibits it from renting or leasing property, buildings or other facilities without approval of the Bradley County Commission, said Buddy Presley, an attorney for the plaintiffs.
The commission did not give that approval, he said.
Presley said the partnership deal is also prohibited by the state constitution.

"The Tennessee State constitution is very clear. It says the state cannot own any entity or corporation with other individuals because that can drive away competition. I'm saying if the state can't do it, the county can't do it because the county is a political subdivision of the state," Presley said.

The lawsuit was filed in Bradley County Chancery Court on Monday. It asks the court to order the hospital to divest all interest in joint-venture entities. The suit also seeks an injunction barring such deals in the future.
